_readme: Every image here is a licensed stock photograph used as a GENERIC stand-in for
a category, not a photograph of the specific venue. The UI must say so on every
rendered card ('stand-in, not this venue'). When a business owner claims a
listing and supplies their own photo, imageKind becomes 'owner' and the stand-in
Each entry was inspected before being assigned: a bakery gets bread, a bar gets
a bar, a cafe gets an interior. Assigning by guesswork is how the old site ended
up showing Denman Arena as the West End's food identity.
Source: Unsplash (free licence, commercial use permitted, attribution not
required but credited). Downloaded at render size and self-hosted; no third-party
LIMITATION, stated plainly: 20 photographs across 9 categories means venues in
the same category share a stand-in. That is visible. The fix is licensed
per-venue photography or owner uploads, not more stock.

byNeighborhood._note: A street-level exterior reads as a neighbourhood without claiming to be a food photograph.

editorial._note: Hand-picked for the neighbourhood cards. Exterior street scene only.
